desc: https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ex2606-dive10-biology-HD.mp4 While marine life seen during the tenth dive of the 2026 American Samoa ROV + Mapping Exploration expedition wasn’t plentiful, it was present. From amphipods clinging to a dead sponge stalk to sea cucumbers, polychaete worms, and a benthic ctenophore with incredibly long (meters long) feeding tentacles, the dive reinforced that even with the harsh temperatures, pressures, and other conditions found at depths over 5,500 meters (3.4 miles), life still finds a way to thrive at the bottom of the ocean.

desc: https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ex2606-dive10-nodules_HD.mp4 During Dive 10 of the 2026 American Samoa ROV + Mapping Exploration expedition, the team observed very large polymetallic nodules, some as large as 10 centimeters (4 inches) or greater in diameter. Nodules form around hard materials, such as fossilized shark teeth or fragments of rock, slowly accumulating around this nucleus. The large size of the nodules seen during the dive suggest that they may have been growing for a very long time. Video courtesy of NOAA Ocean Exploration, 2026 American Samoa ROV + Mapping Exploration.

title: EX2605 Dive 06 Nodule Field
caption: During Dive 06 of the 2026 Cook Islands ROV Exploration cruise, we encountered a field of dense polymetallic nodules of various sizes and shapes on the seafloor. These nodules form over millions of years, as sediment and minerals accumulate around a hard nucleus made of something like a sediment clump or a shark tooth.

title: Flapjack Octopus
caption: Throughout the 2023 Shakedown + EXPRESS West Coast Exploration expedition, we were treated to numerous octopod sightings. The fan favorite flapjack octopods (Opisthoteuthis californiana) in this video were seen during the final dive of the expedition at a depth of 814 meters (2,671 feet). Video courtesy of NOAA Ocean Exploration, 2023 Shakedown + EXPRESS West Coast Exploration.

desc: https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ex2606-dive12-sponge_HD.mp4 During Dive 12 of the 2026 American Samoa ROV + Mapping Exploration expedition, the team encountered this sponge, Caulophacus oxydiscus, that towered an impressive +3 meters tall (9.8 feet) with a head that was 50 centimeters (20 inches) across. The sponge was growing almost perpendicular to the seafloor, rising into the water column to gain better access to food floating by. Video courtesy of NOAA Ocean Exploration, 2026 American Samoa ROV + Mapping Exploration.

title: Anemone
caption: An anemone (Relicanthus daphneae) with its tentacles flowing in the current. This individual was seen in a crack on a sheer rock face on Kaʻena Slope during Dive 08 of the 2025 ROV and Mapping Shakedown expedition. Dive 08 was one of two dives focused on testing a new lighting system with the cameras on remotely operated vehicle Deep Discoverer. Video courtesy of NOAA Ocean Exploration, 2025 Beyond the Blue.
